launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-notes
description: Cloud Notes — our own signed build (the local-first notes/whiteboard app), vendored at ac_cloud-notes/ as owned code. DE-CLOUDED (#469): no sync server, no Firebase/telemetry, no AI chat, no EE-licensed code. The one feature added over upstream is opening files from emulated storage (/storage/emulated/0/...) reached via the fleet rule about EAR discipline — see the ship workflow and testers.
_doc_vendored_engine: Byte-identical to ac_cloud-notes/build.sh, enforced by cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh parity check so the shipped engine and the vendored copy cannot drift.

android._doc_min_sdk: 26, not upstream's 24 (#743): libs:core and libs:devtools declare minSdk 26, and the manifest merger refuses a library whose minSdk is above the app's. Gradle reads the number from gradle/libs.versions.toml::minSdk (variables.gradle), which says the same.
android._doc_gradle_module: Path (app-relative) of the Gradle module that builds the APK. EVERY other app in this fleet keeps it at ./app, so test-app-names-pattern.sh T6 hardcoded that convention and looked for <dir>/app/build.gradle — which this app has never had, because the Android project is nested inside the vendored monorepo. T6 therefore SKIPPED this app in silence, which is exactly how a launcher tile with the wrong label shipped behind 18 green checks (#522). The path is DATA now; T6 reads it and falls back to "app" for everyone else.
android._doc_application_id: FLIPPED (#495): this app now IS Cloud Notes, replacing Markor (formerly ac_cloud-notes, now deleted). #469 shipped it alongside the live Markor under its earlier, since retired application id on purpose, to avoid ripping out a live app and a 9000-file vendor in one commit; #495 is the flip that was always the documented next step. namespace is app.cloudnotes.pro (renamed from the upstream package in #1091) — never shipped as install identity.
android._doc_version: 164/0.27.5 (#495). version_code must exceed ac_cloud-notes's last shipped 163 or the fleet updater's downgrade guard refuses to install this as an update over the device's existing Cloud Notes (observed live: 'stale candidate for notes: versionCode 1 is OLDER than the installed 163') — the vendored Gradle defaults to versionCode 1 with no wiring to this file, which is the defect #495 fixes below. version_name FOLLOWS THE UPSTREAM'S OWN VERSIONING (package.json version at the pinned revision) rather than continuing Markor's Apache-tag-mirroring scheme (163/2.16.1 mirrored upstream Markor tag v2.16.1) — the two apps have unrelated release trains and there is nothing for a post-flip Cloud Notes to mirror from Markor any more. Read into Gradle by app/build.gradle via JsonSlurper (see that file) — this is the ONE declaration; nothing else states these numbers. BUMPED TO 165 (#522): the fleet updater compares versionCode and will not offer an update that is not strictly newer, so a rebuild that kept 164 would fix the name and the logging in the repository and leave the owner's phone on the same bytes it has now. 164 is what run 5ba51c1ce published and what is installed today. The applicationId is UNCHANGED (com.diegonmarcos.cloudnotes since #495), so 165 installs straight over it as an ordinary update — no uninstall, no data loss. BUMPED TO 166 (#743) for the same reason: the APK now carries libs:core's fleet mesh membership, and only a strictly newer code reaches the phone. BUMPED TO 167: 166 crashed on launch (the resource shrinker stripped the ic_nav_* drawables looked up by name; res/raw/keep_nav_icons.xml keeps them), and only a strictly newer code replaces it on the phone. BUMPED TO 168 (#1091): the rename of the packages, crates and native library changes the shipped payload (libcloud_notes_mobile_native.so), and only a strictly newer code reaches the phone.

upstream._doc: Full clone vendored as owned code (no .git, no upstream remote). MIT except packages/backend + packages/common/native — BOTH PRUNED (EE licence forbids copying/distributing). Proven at the Cargo level in ac_cloud-notes/VENDORING-LICENCE.md and enforced by the licence-boundary-guard on every push.

modules._doc: Shared gradle modules the vendored Android project (android.gradle_module's root, packages/frontend/apps/android/App) includes BY REFERENCE beside its own :app. Its settings.gradle iterates this map and, like every other reader of it (the ship workflow's trigger derivation, the publish gate, ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/shared-modules.test.sh), resolves each dir against THIS directory, not against the gradle root five levels down. libs:devtools looks for build.json by walking UP from the gradle root (packages/frontend/apps/android/App), and THIS file is the first one it meets, five levels up: one declaration, no copy and no symlink. A symlink at App/build.json is not an option here: the licence-boundary guard scans packages/frontend/apps/android, follows it, and reads this file's own upstream._doc naming the pruned EE directories as a new reach.

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership (#743): core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission (defined and requested). Declared so a core change rebuilds this app instead of shipping a stale mesh member.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>); not linked directly. Listed so its changes also trigger a rebuild, and because Gradle resolves core's project path against this app's settings.gradle.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: #868 the fleet's bottom island + top page tabs (NavDecl, PageTabsView), shared BY REFERENCE. Cloud Notes draws its five-way nav (Home | Pages | Canvas | Graph | Search) with it from ui.* above and drives the WebView through the cloud-notes:nav event.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1164 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE: Cloud Notes' shell (NotesShell) is the first row, second row, bottom nav and page background of the fleet.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1164 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE: Cloud Notes' shell (NotesShell) is the first row, second row, bottom nav and page background of the fleet.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ai._doc_dir: The top bar's AI panel (and the Search > Ask page): the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) over the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only). Shared BY REFERENCE. This app holds no OpenRouter token and reads none (decisions-use guard D5): the gateway holds the fleet key. Its mesh address is baked as BuildConfig.AI_GATEWAY_URL by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle (ext.aiFleetRoot names the repository root: this Android project is nested).

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency: the shared agent descriptor its Agent picker lists. Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

ui._doc_nav: #868 THE NAVIGATION IS ONE DECLARATION, drawn by the shared nav scaffold of #1164 (bottom nav = ui.bottom_nav, second row = ui.sections[].pages; NotesShell). Cloud Notes is 'Miro + Notion + Obsidian' in one app (a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-notes-hybrid.md); the five bottom items are the five ways in: Home (recent, daily note) | Pages (Notion-style docs: all, tags, collections, new) | Canvas (Miro-style edgeless boards) | Graph (Obsidian-style: global, local, tags) | Search (find, ask/AI). Only ids live here: the web half (core/src/mobile/components/native-nav-routes.ts) maps every `<section>/<page>` to a Cloud Notes workbench route or action, and test/test-nav-routes.sh fails if the two drift. A page with a non-blank `action` is a LAUNCH tab (creates something) and leaves the strip where it was. Settings/Profile are not a bottom item: they are the first row's Configs and Profile icons (Profile launches Cloud Account, extapp:cloud-account), so the bar keeps five equal cells. Every section and page declares a libs:ui-icons catalog icon (SubPageIconGuardTest).
ui._doc_nav_ui: The nav mode Cloud Notes starts in: CLEAN (a transparent first row with only the hamburger, no second row, a compact icons-only bottom nav; the left drawer holds the page dropdown, the AI / Profile / Settings icons and the child-page dropdown). Declared once here, baked as UI_NAV_UI_B64, read by NavUiDecl.fromBuildConfig; the user can switch to Classic in Configs > UI (the choice is persisted per app). scroll_hide: a downward scroll hides every bar until an upward one.

vault._doc: Cloud Notes as the fleet's open Obsidian (Notion + Obsidian + Canvas). EVERYTHING the Vault view does is read from here: how a folder is opened, which files open in which viewer, the panes, the commands, the sandbox policy, the default plugin set. The web half reads the generated mirror core/src/mobile/vault/vault-decl.json (written by scripts/gen-vault-decl.py, which also writes docs/vault-plugin-mapping.md; test/test-vault.sh fails on drift). Obsidian config in the opened folder (<folder>/.obsidian) is only READ and SHOWN in this milestone; applying it is next.

open._doc: Three ways to a folder. saf: ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE with a persisted tree URI (works for any folder the user picks). path: a direct path under direct_roots (needs All files access, like the file explorer). store: a clone in the fleet's shared store, reached through its ContentProvider (the same route Cloud Drive's StoreAccess falls back to when it is not on the shared uid); owner_package, authority and permission are pinned to ac_cloud-termux/build.json::shared_store.provider by test/test-vault.sh, and the store route is unverified on a device until the phone check.

layout._doc: The Obsidian shell inside the content area; the app chrome (top bar, bottom nav) stays the shared nav's. ribbon = the left icon strip, left_panes = tabs of the left sidebar, right_panes = tabs of the right sidebar, status = status bar items. Icons are names the Vault view draws itself.

commands.label: Allow or block CDN scripts in HTML pages

html._doc: A page renders in an iframe with an opaque origin: sandbox has allow-scripts only (no same-origin, forms, popups, top navigation, downloads), and a CSP inside the document. Offline by default: default-src none, so a CDN script or font is blocked. cdn.default false; the toggle (per tab, never remembered across vaults) adds ONLY the hosts listed here, for scripts, styles and fonts. The vault's book (2.1.1) loads Tailwind from cdn.tailwindcss.com and Inter from Google Fonts; both are listed.

vault.plugins_doc: Obsidian plugin to Cloud Notes feature. status: builtin = delivered in the app now, planned = on the roadmap (the plugin is listed as not yet supported), na = not applicable (hosted service, desktop-only, or owned by another fleet app). The default set is the union of the core and community plugins enabled in cloud-me-pvt-notes and git-repos-master; test/test-vault.sh fails when a plugin enabled in either vault is missing here.

artifact_assert._doc: Read by cloud-notes-engine.sh::_assert_apk_payload (#513). The ship pipeline could not tell a working app from a blank one: gradle builds a perfectly valid APK around an empty assets/public/, signs it, and CI goes green. These are the floors the BUILT ARTIFACT must clear — bytes and presence, never a filename in a manifest. Set far below what a healthy build produces (observed on the published APK: index.html 2696 B, 114 chunks / 31.2 MB of JS, libcloud_notes_mobile_native.so 51.8 MB) so a real regression trips them and normal upstream churn does not.
artifact_assert._doc_required_globs: #522: the two payload files the FIRST LAUNCH cannot proceed without, named because the first launch is where this app has failed twice. app.tsx opens the local document store with `new Worker(getWorkerUrl(nbstore))`, and core/src/utils/first-app-data.ts bootstraps the first workspace with `fetch(onboardingUrl)` over the bundled onboarding template. Either one absent and createFirstAppData() rejects, the rejection is caught in core/src/desktop/pages/index/index.tsx, and the owner is shown "An internal error occurred." behind a green CI run. Globs, not literal names, because both carry a content hash / a version.
artifact_assert._doc_kotlin_binding: #522: the committed UniFFI binding, asserted against the SHIPPED .so by test-launch-payload.sh. #469 hand-edited this file to drop hashcash_mint and cut two lines too many, leaving `uniffi_cloud_notes_mobile_native_fn_func_new_doc_storage_pool` CALLED but never DECLARED and an orphan `): Pointer` in the interface body — committed Kotlin that does not parse. Nothing noticed, because Gradle regenerates the file from the built .so before javaCompile (the generate<Variant>UniFFIBindings task, which #469 believed was a no-op). A committed source that is never the source that builds is a trap with a fuse on it.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Notes as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-notes-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-notes-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: Shell testers under ac_cloud-notes/test/ that prove licence-cleanliness and app identity WITHOUT a build. Read by cloud-android-test-engine.sh::tests.shell.

root_scope._doc: Read by test/test-root-scope-services.sh (#513). entrypoint is the file whose every render happens on the ROOT framework provider; module_roots are the trees walked to DERIVE which services are registered under a .scope(...) and are therefore unresolvable there. Paths live here, never in the tester.

capacitor_surface._doc: Read by test/test-capacitor-plugin-surface.sh (#543). web_root is the tree walked to DERIVE which Capacitor plugin NAMES this app's bundle calls (registerPlugin<T>('Name')); activity is the ONE file that registers their native implementations; kotlin_root is where the @CapacitorPlugin(name = "...") annotations are read from. No plugin name is ever written in the tester — a missing native side must be derived, because that is the defect (#543: the web side called 'Auth', the de-clouding had deleted the native class, and Capacitor threw 'plugin is not implemented on android' on the LOCAL workspace path).

html_import._doc: Read by test/test-html-import-route.sh (#547). entrypoint is where an opened file is dispatched to an importer; native_plugin is the ONE file declaring which extensions the device will read (its SUPPORTED set); converter is upstream's HtmlTransformer source, read to derive the options importHTMLToDoc accepts. Which extensions ARE html is derived from Python's built-in MIME table, never written in the tester.

file_explorer._doc: Read by test/test-file-explorer.sh (#547). entrypoint is where the explorer renders and picks a file; plugin_ts is the web-side plugin type; native_plugin is the Kotlin class that must implement every method that type declares; activity is where the FAB dispatches the event the explorer listens for. Method and event names are DERIVED from these files, never written in the tester.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json). general.sections: the anchors and sections of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs). about: what the app does, its features, privacy and the fleet services it talks to (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time). Name, icon, version, build sha, repo, licence, crash sink and debug API are derived, never typed here.

about.what: Local-first notes and whiteboards: pages, canvases, a graph of links and search, with no sync server and no telemetry.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.
